teaser.en: Sticks from this shrub catch octopus on the reef, but burn it at home and, it is said, you risk leprosy.

summary.en: *Mvua pweza*, the 'octopus fisher', is a coastal bush shrub with yellow flowers and black fruits on a bright red base. Its sticks are used to catch octopus, but it must never be burned or built with.

about.en: *Mvua pweza* is a shrub of the Ochna family, the plants often called Mickey Mouse bushes. Its flowers are yellow. After flowering, the sepals and the swollen base of the flower turn bright red, and the black fruits sit on top like eyes, a striking red-and-black display.

where.en: It grows in coastal bushland, close enough to the shore for its sticks to be carried down to the reef.

uses.en: Its sticks are used to catch octopus on the reef.

culture.en: Its two names point in opposite directions. *Mvua pweza* means 'octopus fisher', after its use at sea. *Mtsonga mahana* means 'causer of leprosy': using it for firewood or for building is believed to cause leprosy, so it is kept out of the home.

names.en: Pakia records two Digo names, *mvua pweza* and *mtsonga mahana*. No Swahili or English common name has been recorded; botanists call it *Ochna thomasiana*.

reason.en: Another shrub never used for firewood because of a belief
Also avoided for building because of a belief
Another shrub used for catching animals
Also carries a 'mtsonga' (maker or causer) name
